body: As this will invalidate translations, let's merge for 4.5-dev1, so translators have enough time to handle the fuzzy strings before 4.5-stable.
Thanks! Congratulations on your first merged contribution! 🎉

I noticed these changes when doing translation and I think they are unnecessary.

I can understand changing `1` to `1.0` in the body of the description to make it easier to distinguish floating-point numbers. But sample code is... code. Many people tend to write `1.0` as `1` in everyday programming, unless the compiler does not allow it (e.g., when writing shaders).

A lot of existing sample code passes string literals for `StringName` and `NodePath` arguments  (writing `"something"` rather than `^"something"` or `&"something"`). This is simply because they are converted automatically and users don't need to care about such difference in actual programming.

I have kept this PR in mind as having been a mistake. It's not just for the reasons highlighted above, the pass in this PR is genuinely inconsistent. Only `1` are affected, other amounts in seconds are not. Neither are other values passed that are also floats. I would seriously consider reverting this, but the (mild) damage to localization has already been done.

> A lot of existing sample code passes string literals for `StringName` and `NodePath` arguments (writing `"something"` rather than `^"something"` or `&"something"`). This is simply because they are converted automatically and users don't need to care about such difference in actual programming.

Indeed, I actively discourage explicit literals in GDScript, unless it's absolutely necessary for the example provided.

Personally I think it's good practice to be explicit about floats in one's code, especially given the (to some users, surprising) behavior of Godot with integer division. If there are some other whole floats in that class which don't have `.0` suffix, they should likely be changed too.

The documentation needs to be consistent and to me the most consistent style for floats in docs is to include a decimal point. This is actually covered in the GDScript style guide, which I would argue the documentation should follow:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_styleguide.html#numbers

For example this was totally inconsistent even within a single method call:
```
tween.tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 200.0, 1).as_relative()
```

I agree the churn on translations isn't great, but now it's merged and done and going back might not really help, unless I spend time manually reflagging translations as non-fuzzy, but that would imply checking which ones were fuzzied by that change or were fuzzied earlier... honestly it's simpler to just fix translations when you encounter those.

Ah, it's not about the extra translation work :P

I'm perfectly fine if it's changing 1 to 1.0 in some description, like `Returns [code]1.0[/code] if the node is visible` because our _writing_ style do use that to hint that the return value is a `float`.

But for _coding_ style, there's nothing wrong passing an `int` for a `float` parameter. When coding, adding the trailing `.0` usually shows that you do want to achieve something:

```gdscript
# I want to avoid integer division
print(42.0 / variable)

# I want to be consistent with the code around me
tween.tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 200, 1.5)
tween.tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 300, 1.0) # <---
tween.tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 400, 2.8)

# I want to avoid some buggy behavior
# (the tween's dest value must match the property's exact type in the early days of the new tween)
tween.tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 200.0, duration)

# I want my shader to compile
COLOR = some_variable * 3.0

# Reader confused: why does the author want to emphasize that the last argument is a float?
tween.tween_property($Sprite, "scale", Vector2(), 1.0)
```

The GDScript style guide section is about omitting the leading/trailing zero while still preserving the decimal point. It requires `1.` to be written as `1.0` to minimize the possibility of it being mistaken for `1`. It's a problem that `1` doesn't have. `1` can't be mistaken as a float, and passing an int for a float parameter is supported.

I just realized that we can avoid similar situations in the future by using non-integral values. This not only allows showing that the parameter is a floating-point number, but also avoids the `.0` suffix that is not commonly used in real programming :smile: 

```gdscript
tween.tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 200.0, 1.5).as_relative()
```

> r. When coding, adding the trailing `.0` usually shows that you do want to achieve something:

I don't see it this way. For me adding a trailing `.0` means I want to be explicit in my code (for myself / team mates) that this is a float.

There should be no coding style difference to me between `2.0` and `2.1`. They're both floats and they should be written the same way.

I think it comes down to personal preference but for the docs we need consistency, and it's IMO much more consistent to say "always include `.0` for whole floats so that they're consistent with any other float" than "leave it out for whole floats to be inconsistent with other floats".

> I just realized that we can avoid similar situations in the future by using non-integral values. This not only allows showing that the parameter is a floating-point number, but also avoids the `.0` suffix that is not commonly used in real programming 😄

Citation needed that Real Programmers™ don't use the `.0` suffix :P I use it all the time. We also use it as a policy in C++ to make the type explicit (not necessarily consistently as it's hard to enforce, but it's our recommended way to write floats/doubles).

> ```
> # I want my shader to compile
> COLOR = some_variable * 3.0
> ```

Exactly, and we fixed enough critical regressions where rendering would break due to this habit of Real Programmers™ that I think we should fight it with proper float writing guidelines.

It's also important for type inference, etc. It's just much simpler to be consistent IMO.
Either way, this PR needs a follow-up because it's not been applied consistently, on this page alone at least.
